subject: Local and global names
notes: kb/Work PB1047 (w68z). cite.py --check 8.4.6.2.1 'Using this set of names, the normal rules for qualification and any other rules for uniqueness of reference are applied until one or more items is identified' -> OK §8.4.6.2.1 1); cite.py --check 8.4.6.2.2 'All data-names and screen-names subordinate to a global name are global names' -> OK. The GLOBAL-root loop skipped a container root whose SPELLING the unit already had and dropped its WHOLE subtree, so a subordinate global name of a shadowed root (lg11 Y, lg12 Z) was 'not defined'. BindUnitData now inherits every global root whole; a local root spelled like one takes a distinct C# member (ReserveInheritedMemberNames) so the root's bridge can be emitted. Golden: I Y=OUY and I Z=OUZ W=MDW (subordinates of the outer G, whose spelling the middle's G hides), and O Y=NEW (the contained program's MOVE reached the outer item through the bridge).
